chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: On Shane's comment, for the HTTPS/SVCB RFC 9460 we went through this and landed on including "http/1.1" by default implicitly in the default alpn list and then having a no-default-alpn SvcParam. This was after lots of discussion, and the strong desire from some folks was to have a "safe" default lacking operational footguns.

chat.author: Peter van Dijk
chat.text: Over lunch the SVCB comparison also came up

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: (The Chrome folks for example said that they would have a safe fallback logic regardless to avoid breakage, without an explicit "I really want to shoot myself in my foot" signal.

chat.author: David Lawrence
chat.text: OTOH I'm still biased toward "if you're specifying transports, make it all explicit."

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: Well good we don't have browser folk implementing DNS resolvers :troll:

chat.author: Petr Špaček
chat.text: I'm with Tale and Pieter - better explicit than implicit.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Hm. So for consistency with SVCB having a no53 makes sense, but then we'd also need noadot and noadoq...

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Personally I prefer a design where if you list transports, list all the ones that you support...

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: I'm not arguing we should do the same here, just explaining the background for why SVCB (specifically HTTPS RR) landed where it did.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: But DNS is so crufty I wouldn't die on that hill.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: @Erik: Ah, okah!

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: Shane: The concern on this bikesehed point is about whether adding "transport=adot" implicitly disables Do53, which was previously implicitly enabled.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: @Ben: yes

chat.author: Gavin Brown
chat.text: @duane: Petr has just come up with another use for CDELEG :)

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text:
The parity for SVCB would be:
 transport=adot,adoq
with an implicit 'do53' always being added to the transport list and then a "no-default-transport" SvcParam that would exclude the do53 from the list.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: And I think it should. Which also gives me what I want, which is "transport=do53" would disable probing for resolvers that care.

chat.author: Pieter Lexis
chat.text: Maybe we need a DNS range in the svcparam registry instead of deleginfo so more reuse can occur

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: Shane: It sounds like you're proposing that the default is not "Do53", but rather "who knows? Try and find out".  That seems messy to me, requiring every resolver to have probing capabilities.

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text:
I mean... the default today is YOLO.
With DELEG, we could make the default YOLO, but if transports are specified then the transports are what is specified.
